verses.text: Of Moab. Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo! for it is laid waste; Kiriathaim is disappointed, it is taken; Misgab  is put to shame and broken down.

The praise of Moab is no more; in Heshbon they have devised evil against her: ‘Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation.’ You also, Madmen, will be brought to silence. The sword will pursue you.
The sound of a cry from Horonaim, desolation and great destruction!
Moab is destroyed. Her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
For they shall go up by the ascent of Luhith with continual weeping. For at the descent of Horonaim they have heard the distress of the cry of destruction.
Flee! Save your lives! Be like the juniper bush in the wilderness.
For, because you have trusted in your works and in your treasures, you also shall be taken. Chemosh will go out into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
The destroyer will come on every city, and no city will escape; the valley also will perish, and the plain will be destroyed; as Yahweh has spoken.
Give wings to Moab, that she may fly and get herself away: and her cities will become a desolation, without anyone to dwell in them.
“Cursed is he who does the work of Yahweh negligently; and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from blood.

“Moab has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his lees, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither has he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remains in him, and his scent is not changed.
Therefore behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will send to him those who pour off, and they shall pour him off; and they shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles in pieces.
Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence.
“How do you say, ‘We are mighty men, and valiant men for the war?’
Moab is laid waste, and they have gone up into his cities, and his chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter,” says the King, whose name is Yahweh of Armies.
“The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hurries fast.
All you who are around him, bemoan him, and all you who know his name; say, ‘How is the strong staff broken, the beautiful rod!’
“You daughter who dwells in Dibon, come down from your glory, and sit in thirst; for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you, he has destroyed your strongholds.
Inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and watch: ask him who flees, and her who escapes; say, ‘What has been done?’
Moab is disappointed; for it is broken down. Wail and cry! Tell it by the Arnon, that Moab is laid waste.
Judgment has come on the plain country, on Holon, and on Jahzah, and on Mephaath,
and on Dibon, and on Nebo, and on Beth Diblathaim,
and on Kiriathaim, and on Beth Gamul, and on Beth Meon,
and on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, and on all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,” says Yahweh.
“Make him drunken; for he magnified himself against Yahweh: and Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
For wasn’t Israel a derision to you? was he found among thieves? for as often as you speak of him, you shake your head.
You inhabitants of Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock; and be like the dove that makes her nest over the mouth of the abyss.
“We have heard of the pride of Moab. He is very proud; his loftiness, and his pride, and his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.
I know his wrath,” says Yahweh, “that it is nothing; his boastings have worked nothing.
Therefore I will wail for Moab. Yes, I will cry out for all Moab. They shall mourn for the men of Kir Heres.

With more than the weeping of Jazer will I weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches passed over the sea. They reached even to the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruits and on your vintage.
Gladness and joy is taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab. I have caused wine to cease from the wine presses. No one will tread with shouting. The shouting will be no shouting.
From the cry of Heshbon even to Elealeh, even to Jahaz have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even to Horonaim, to Eglath Shelishiyah: for the waters of Nimrim also will become desolate.
Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab,” says Yahweh, “him who offers in the high place, and him who burns incense to his gods.
Therefore my heart sounds for Moab like pipes, and my heart sounds like pipes for the men of Kir Heres. Therefore the abundance that he has gotten has perished.
For every head is bald, and every beard clipped. There are cuttings on all the hands, and sackcloth on the waist.
On all the housetops of Moab, and in its streets, there is lamentation everywhere; for I have broken Moab like a vessel in which no one delights,” says Yahweh.
“How it is broken down! How they wail! How Moab has turned the back with shame! So shall Moab become a derision and a terror to all who are around him.”
For Yahweh says: “Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread out his wings against Moab.
Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are seized. The heart of the mighty men of Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.
Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he has magnified himself against Yahweh.
Terror, the pit, and the snare are on you, inhabitant of Moab,” says Yahweh.
“He who flees from the terror will fall into the pit; and he who gets up out of the pit will be taken in the snare: for I will bring on him, even on Moab, the year of their visitation,” says Yahweh.

“Those who fled stand without strength under the shadow of Heshbon; for a fire has gone out of Heshbon, and a flame from the middle of Sihon, and has devoured the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh are undone; for your sons are taken away captive, and your daughters into captivity.
“Yet I will bring back the captivity of Moab in the latter days,” says Yahweh.  Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

footnotes.content: God's word opens against Moab with the weight of loss already declared—cities we read as names on maps were homes to people. When the Lord speaks 'woe,' it marks the end of an age, not a whisper. Notice that shame precedes loss; pride cracks first, then the walls follow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In Heshbon, enemies gather in council to unmake a nation. The bitter truth here: we often help destroy what we should defend. Madmen will be silenced—those who plot against God's purposes discover that the sword pursues them instead.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Horonaim's cry echoes across the valleys—whole regions wailing at once. Desolation and great destruction ride together. The sound itself becomes a witness to what God has allowed to unfold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the little ones cry out—a nation's ruin reaches into the nurseries. There is tenderness in God's word here too: He does not hide the suffering He permits, nor does He call it good. Judgment is grievous work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The road up Luhith flows with tears, and at its base stands only distress and ruin. When a people must flee the only home they know, their weeping rises like a prayer the Lord does hear—even judgment is met with divine attention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To flee like a juniper in the wilderness—stripped bare, alone, but enduring. The command to save your lives carries a thread of mercy even in judgment: run, choose life, scatter rather than perish in one place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Trust in works and treasures—the old lie. Chemosh goes into captivity; the god they trusted cannot save, and his priests and princes go with him. When we lean on what cannot hold us, we fall into judgment ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No city will escape—not one. The destroyer sweeps both valley and plain. When God has spoken a judgment, His word will accomplish it. There is no negotiating, no sanctuary built by human hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Give Moab wings to flee—a bitter wish. The land becomes empty, cities stand vacant. There is something haunting about a city no one chooses to live in, haunted by the absence of life that once filled it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cursed be the hand that shrinks from the Lord's work. This verse shows us judgment is not reluctant cruelty but a necessary enforcement of the moral order. To withhold the sword when God has spoken is itself a rebellion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab at ease from youth, settled, undisturbed like wine on its lees—unchanging, complacent. We grow comfortable in our sins when the Lord is patient, and forget that patience is not permission. The taste of our pride stays in our mouth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now He sends those who pour off the wine, to empty the vessels and break the bottles. What was treasured becomes waste. Comfort ends; complacency breaks like pottery.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab ashamed of Chemosh as Israel was ashamed of Bethel—a hard echo across generations. The confidence we place in false gods becomes our deepest shame when judgment comes. Yet this mirrors Israel's own path, calling both to repentance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The boast of the mighty rings hollow when the Lord speaks against them: 'We are valiant men for war.' Pride speaks thus, just before the silence comes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chosen young men—the best, the brightest—go down to slaughter. This is not mercy; this is the full weight of what rejecting God costs. Yet even here, Yahweh of Armies speaks: the King Himself rules this ruin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Calamity rushes; affliction hastens. There is no time to prepare, no moment to turn back. This is what it means when the Lord sets His hand against a people hardened in their sin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All around him wail—neighbors and those who knew his name weep for the broken staff, the beautiful rod gone dark. When a nation falls, the whole region feels the loss. There is an odd tenderness in grief, even for the enemy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dibon's daughter—personified as a woman stripped of glory, thrust from her high place to sit in thirst. The destroyer has come; strongholds fall. Such language honors the realness of loss.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The inhabitant of Aroer watches the road for news—asking the fleeing ones what happened. In catastrophe, we hunger to know if there was any escape, any survival. The watcher stands by the way, waiting to hear.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab disappointed—broken. The cry spreads by the Arnon; the word travels—Moab is laid waste. Bad news moves fast, carried by those who watched it happen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The plain country receives judgment—Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath all named. God knows the places; He calls them by name as judgment falls. Not one city escapes His notice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dibon, Nebo, Beth Diblathaim—more cities enumerated, more names standing witness to the sweep of judgment. Each city listed is real; each was a home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kiriathaim, Beth Gamul, Beth Meon—the catalogue continues. The repetition itself speaks: everywhere, everywhere, everywhere. There is no corner left untouched.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the cities of Moab—far or near—receive the judgment. Whether distant or adjacent, whether great or small, all fall under one sentence. The sweep is total.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The horn of Moab is cut off, the arm broken—strength made useless. This is the language of disarming: what Moab relied on for power is now dead. The Lord speaks it so.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Make him drunken—let him taste his own poison, wallowing in his vomit. The mockery is fierce because the magnifying of self against the Lord is the root sin. Shame follows the pride.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: You mocked Israel as a thief; you shook your head at him. Now the Lord turns the derision back: you will become a derision yourself. What we mock, we become.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Leave the cities; dwell in the rock. Be like the dove that nests over the abyss's mouth—hidden, clinging, alive but barely. Sometimes survival means abandoning home, choosing precarious shelter over proud ruin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We have heard of Moab's pride—it spreads like a bad report, loftiness, arrogance, haughtiness of heart. Pride is a voice that carries; everyone hears it. And everyone waits to see it fall.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I know his wrath; it is nothing—boastings have worked nothing. God speaks the truth of pride: it is empty air, accomplishing nothing real. The loud voice makes no purchase on the world when the Lord has spoken against it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Therefore I will wail for Moab—the Lord Himself weeps. Even in judgment, there is this tenderness, this sorrow. He grieves what He must break. The men of Kir Heres will be mourned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: With more than the weeping of Jazer—the vine of Sibmah, branches reaching to the sea, summer fruits and vintage all fallen to the destroyer. This is the language of agricultural loss, of wine turned to grief, of abundance made nothing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gladness is taken away; wine ceases in the presses. No one treads with shouting—the vintage festivals die. When joy disappears, the land knows it has been abandoned by the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From Heshbon to Elealeh, Jahaz to Zoar, Horonaim to Eglath Shelishiyah—voices uttering their despair across the whole land. The waters of Nimrim desolate too. Geography itself becomes a map of grief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: I will cause to cease him who offers in the high place, who burns incense to his gods. Even the priests and their rituals fall silent. The sound of worship dies; the gods remain deaf.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: My heart sounds like pipes for Moab—a mournful instrument plays the dirge for what is lost. The abundance gotten is gone. The Lord Himself grieves, and His grief is its own kind of judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every head bald, every beard clipped, cuttings on the hands, sackcloth on the waist—the visible marks of mourning, raw signs of anguish. The whole nation wears its grief openly.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: On all the housetops and streets, lamentation everywhere. The Lord has broken Moab like a vessel no one wants. The image is intimate and terrible: a broken pot, worthless, discarded.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: How it is broken down! How they wail! Moab has turned the back with shame. The repeated question—how?—echoes the incomprehension of those who watched a nation fall. Shame is complete.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He shall fly as an eagle, spread out his wings against Moab—the image of swift judgment, irresistible power descending. There is no escape from wings spread wide across the sky.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kerioth is taken, strongholds seized. The mighty men's hearts become as a woman in labor pangs—an image of terror and helplessness. Strength means nothing when the Lord has turned against you.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moab shall be destroyed from being a people—ceasing to exist as a nation. Because he magnified himself against the Lord. This is the final cost of pride: erasure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Terror, the pit, and the snare are on you—three traps that close in. There is no room to move, no corner that is safe. The inhabitant of Moab faces an inescapable judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He who flees terror falls into the pit; he who escapes the pit is caught in the snare. Every direction holds only another judgment. This is what it means when the Lord brings His year of visitation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who fled stand without strength under Heshbon's shadow; a fire from Sihon devours Moab's corner and the heads of the tumultuous. Nowhere to hide, no strength left to run. The judgment is fire.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh are undone—sons taken captive, daughters into captivity. The families are torn apart; the future is broken. The god Chemosh cannot save his people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yet I will bring back the captivity of Moab in the latter days—mercy whispers after judgment thunders. Readers today hear an echo in this word: judgment is not God's final word. Even broken nations can be restored when the Lord chooses restoration. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
